h2: Work that refuses to sit still.
Hire me for one of these
No briefs lost in email. Just this.
p: Scroll-driven stories, custom cursors and interfaces with a pulse. Design and code, same pair of hands.
Scroll-driven stories, custom cursors, and interfaces with a pulse.

A social-first creative agency site with a paper plane that flies you through the page. Gate screen, custom cursor, editorial collage in forest green, cream and pink — and a GSAP-driven plane that hops section to section before unfolding into a letter.
Scroll-scrubbed hero video for a Shopify theme. When Safari refused to seek cleanly, I rebuilt the whole effect as a canvas frame sequence — same cinema, none of the stutter.
A cinematic scroll-driven product story for a supplement brand, built from AI-generated footage and scrubbed frame by frame. Part film, part interface.
Nine ScrollTrigger scenes for a premium suiting house: fabric unrolls, seams stitch themselves, the jacket assembles as you read. My playground for tailored motion.
An invitation you scroll. Arch-shaped portraits as a site-wide motif, frosted glass event cards and an alternating timeline that unfolds across two days in Rajasthan.
Mostwebsiteshandyouinformation.Iwouldratherbuildthekindyou*fallinto*—wherethescrollhasaplot,thecursorhasopinions,andnothingimportantis*boring*.
Pinned scenes, scrubbed video, sections that hand off to each other. The scroll bar as a plot device.
I don't hand a design to someone else and hope. The Figma file and the running site are the same decision.
Real sites for real businesses — themes bent past what the theme editor allows, without breaking checkout.
Type, palette, motion language, and the small stupid detail that makes a site feel like someone made it.

h2: Product work, with the numbers attached
Where AI actually shows up in my work
Point me at a messy program.
p: Product Manager, 3+ years across B2B SaaS and AI. I take a fuzzy commercial goal, turn it into a program with owners, a tracker and a number to beat — then run it. Hands-on with APIs, SQL and the analytics, so nobody has to translate for me.
Goodproductworkusuallylooksboringfromtheoutside.Atrackersomebodyactuallyupdates.Adashboardsalesopenswithoutmeintheroom.Apipelinethatoutlivesthepersonwhobuiltit.That'sthewholejob.

Growth was spread thin across five micromarkets with no shared view of which cohorts actually mattered — and almost nobody ordered in the app. Roughly 3% of the network used it; the rest still bought offline.

Segmented the base by cohort, built margin-aware discount ladders and ran full-funnel AARRR analytics. Migrated offline purchasers into in-app ordering with targeted lifecycle campaigns, and led a three-phase go-to-market launch for a new product line across product design, marketing, sales and customer success.

An analytics dashboard centralising KPI reporting across every market, and an automated end-to-end communication pipeline — AI cohort segmentation, triggered lifecycle campaigns, KPI reporting — replacing manual ops with always-on engagement. Plus the RRDC-2 rewards ladder and the operator's playbook the team runs on.
Given to independent experts for what they contribute back to the developer community. Renewed each year, most recently through 2027.
My career mentorship work put up in Times Square. It went live while I was on the flight home; I found out two days later, on landing.
Awarded to support open-source contributors early in their work — the same year as my first Google Summer of Code.
I know what a selection panel is looking for because I've sat on one — the first time before I'd graduated.
Conference halls, campuses and one booth in Chicago — pegged up as they happened.
Four countries, six cities — talks, a booth and one billboard.
Reels, shorts and posts — the part of the job that happens after the shipping.
Turning a commercial goal into a program with cohorts, ladders, owners and a date it gets reviewed.
Moving a number that the business already cares about — GMV, transacting users, the share of orders that happen in the product.
RFM cohorts, chase-back funnels and 90-day plans aimed at monthly transacting users, not vanity signups.
The dashboard a sales lead opens on their own, without me in the room to explain it.
I scope the integration myself — APIs, auth, data flows — and check feasibility before it becomes someone else's problem.
Coupon stages and loyalty math explained to sales in plain language, and the commercial reality explained back to engineering.
